title: How plateaus wear down into mesas and buttes
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What is the difference between a mesa and a butte?

explain.say: In dry places with flat layers of rock, a hard top layer called caprock can protect the softer rock beneath. A big raised flat area like this is a plateau.

draw.text: How plateaus wear down into mesas and buttes

explain.say: Rivers and flash floods cut into the plateau through cracks. The cracks widen into valleys, cutting off flat-topped hills wider than they are tall, called mesas, from the Spanish word for table.
As the edges keep crumbling, a mesa shrinks into a butte, a narrow hill with steep sides that is taller than it is wide.
Finally a butte wears down to a thin spire, then disappears. Monument Valley in the USA shows every stage of this story side by side.

faq.q: What is the difference between a mesa and a butte?
faq.a: Both are flat-topped hills with steep sides. A mesa is wider than it is tall, like a table. A butte is smaller, taller than it is wide.
A hard caprock protects soft rock below. Water cuts valleys through the plateau, leaving flat-topped hills where the caprock still survives. Their sides crumble as the soft rock below is worn away.
Caprock is a layer of hard rock, like sandstone or basalt, on top of softer rock. It resists erosion and keeps the tops of mesas and buttes flat.
asks: Why do mesas have flat tops?

faq.q: Where can I see mesas and buttes?
faq.a: In dry lands with flat-lying rock layers, especially the south-west USA, like Monument Valley, and also in Australia, Venezuela and parts of Africa.

faq.q: Why do mesas form in deserts?
faq.a: Few plants protect the ground, so rare heavy rains erode fast, and the dry climate keeps the steep cliffs sharp instead of being softened into gentle slopes.
asks: Why are buttes in dry places?

facts: Monument Valley on the Arizona and Utah border is famous for its sandstone buttes.

quiz.say: What keeps the top of a mesa flat?
quiz.show: A mesa's flat top comes from…
quiz.why: Hard caprock resists erosion while softer rock around and below wears away.

wrong.2: Wind does not build flat rock tops.
